subject: Renewal questions: temporary rate cap + grace credits for upcoming pilot surge
messages:

To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchidai.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions: temporary rate cap + grace credits for upcoming pilot surge

Hi Mateo / Vanessa,

Quick context: our Q4 pilot (customer-facing beta) is moving earlier than planned and we expect a usage spike starting Sep 1. We have the renewal coming up Oct 1 and want to avoid a billing surprise.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary rate cap at our current renewal rate for the first 12 months so we have predictable unit costs through 2027?
- Can you provide a short-term grace credit or buffer to cover expected pilot overage in Sept–Nov while we finalize a capacity bump?

I attached our projected usage file and a short PO stub for planning. If possible we need a written offer by Aug 25 so procurement can align with internal billing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if helpful.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Product
OrchidAI

Attachments: OrchidAI_ProjectedUsage_Q3_v3.xlsx, OrchidAI_PO_stub.pdf

Vanessa / Marissa — forwarding OrchidAI. They want a temporary rate cap and a short-term grace credit to cover an expected Sept–Nov surge. Attached their projected usage for reference.

Notes/questions:
- Their renewal date is Oct 1, committed tier today is a 12-month commit at reduced per-token rates.
- If we offer a rate cap, finance will want clear guardrails (max cap exposure, duration).
- Suggest two parallel options to present: (A) 90-day surge credit up to $40k + 12-month rate cap at current renewal rate, or (B) commit acceleration incentive: move to a 12-month upfront commit with a 15% credit applied to the accelerated portion.

Ben — can you quick-run impact (credit budget vs. expected revenue) and flag approvals needed?

I can draft the outbound to Elena once we agree language.

Thanks,
Mateo

Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal questions: temporary rate cap + grace credits for upcoming pilot surge

Good morning — quick guidance.

I like offering a two-path proposal so OrchidAI can choose what fits their cashflow and risk profile. Keep language tight and set an explicit cap on our exposure. Suggested structure:

Option 1 — Pilot Surge Buffer (recommended for pilot customers):
- 90-day grace credit (applies Sep 1–Nov 30) equal to up to $35,000 in overage. Any overage beyond that is billable at their negotiated renewal rate.
- 12-month temporary rate cap: we lock the per-token renewal rate at the current quoted renewal rate for 12 months from Oct 1.
- No change to commit; applies even if they stay on current consumption plan.

Option 2 — Commit Acceleration (higher commitment, deeper incentive):
- If they accelerate to a 12-month committed purchase (prepay or billed monthly but contractually committed) within 30 days, provide a 15% credit on the accelerated portion (applied as invoice credit across first 3 months).
- We can combine a smaller pilot credit ($15k) with the commit incentive.

Approvals: any credit > $30k needs Finance + Sales Leadership sign-off. Ben — please confirm if $35k is within tolerance or if we should cap to $30k for faster approval.

I’ll mark this as a Priority decision; we should respond to Elena with a short, numbered offer and include the temporary rate cap PDF and a link to DocuSign.

-Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@orchidai.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@orchidai.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: two-path renewal offer to cover pilot surge (options A + B)

Hi Elena — thanks for the projection and PO stub. Based on our internal review we can offer two paths; please see the short summary below and the attached formal offer PDF.

Option A — Pilot Surge Buffer (no commitment change):
- 90-day grace credit covering up to $30,000 of overage charges (applies Sep 1–Nov 30).
- Temporary rate cap: we will lock your per-token renewal rate at the current quoted renewal rate for 12 months beginning Oct 1, 2026.
- Terms: grace credit applied as invoice credit after usage is reconciled; standard T&Cs apply.

Option B — Commit Acceleration (preferred if you want price certainty):
- Move to a 12-month committed plan (effective Oct 1) for an accelerated portion of usage; if executed within 30 days we apply a 15% credit on the accelerated commit volume, applied as invoice credit over the first 3 billing periods.
- We can layer a smaller pilot credit ($15,000) to cover transition months.

Logistics & next steps:
1) I attached the Redwood_TemporaryRateCap_Offer.pdf (legal summary).
2) We can issue a DocuSign package for the commit amendment if you pick Option B — link included below.
3) Please confirm which option you prefer by Aug 25 so procurement can finalize their PO. If you accept Option A we’ll send a short amendment confirming the rate cap and credit schedule.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-orchidai-renewal
Attachments: Redwood_TemporaryRateCap_Offer.pdf, OrchidAI_ProjectedUsage_Q3_v3.xlsx

If you want a quick 20-minute call to walk through the options I’m available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference
